title: Sponsorship Violence: A Review of Incidents 2220–2225 — Internal Memorandum, Tier Management Office
body:
GLMZ CITIZEN BENEFITS BUREAU TIER MANAGEMENT OFFICE — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM SUBJECT: SPONSORSHIP VIOLENCE — FIVE-YEAR INCIDENT REVIEW, 2220–2225 CLASSIFICATION: RESTRICTED — TIER 4 MINIMUM ACCESS Prepared by: Statistical Integrity Division Distribution: Bureau Director, Legislative Council Tier Subcommittee, Arcturus Defense Solutions Civil Security Liaison

---

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This memorandum summarizes Sponsorship Violence incidents (as defined under Penal Code Section 14.7 and Administrative Code Article 7.3.5) recorded in the GLMZ between January 2220 and December 2225. The review covers assault, aggravated assault, homicide, threatening communications, and property destruction incidents in which the verified victim was a Sponsoring Citizen and the verified perpetrator was a current or prospective sponsored Citizen.

Total verified incidents (2220–2225): 312 Homicide incidents: 47 Aggravated assault incidents: 89 Assault and threatening communications: 176

Average annual incident rate: 52 incidents per year, representing an increase of 34% over the 2215–2220 period (38.8 incidents/year).

This memorandum is provided to the Legislative Council Tier Subcommittee in advance of the 2226 Tier Protocol Revision deliberations.

---

SELECTED INCIDENT SUMMARIES

The following incidents are presented as representative examples of incident typology. Full incident reports are maintained in the Bureau archive (Tier 5 access required).

INCI-2221-047 City: Chicago (the Gray Zone district 4) Victim: Tier 4 Citizen, employment: senior logistics coordinator, age 52 Perpetrator: Tier 1 Citizen, sponsored Citizen, month 8 of 36-month Sponsorship Period Incident: Perpetrator assaulted victim at victim's registered residence. Victim sustained injuries requiring hospitalization. Perpetrator apprehended at scene. Investigation revealed perpetrator alleged victim had demanded sexual compliance as condition of continued Sponsorship. Bureau note: Allegation made post-arrest, not verified. Victim did not file counter-complaint. Case proceeding under Section 14.7. Perpetrator tier reduced to Tier 1, twenty-year detention. Bureau classification: Sponsorship Violence — Assault.

INCI-2222-103 City: Milwaukee (Kinnickinnic corridor) Victim: Tier 5 Citizen, employment: executive, Tessera Corponation subsidiary, age 61 Perpetrator: Tier 2 Citizen, prospective sponsored Citizen (Sponsorship Agreement not yet signed) Incident: Perpetrator made threatening communications to victim via encrypted relay following victim's decision not to proceed with Sponsorship. Perpetrator had invested eight months in relationship cultivation prior to victim's refusal. Perpetrator apprehended. Bureau note: Threatening communications documented. Perpetrator's Section 14.7 classification was challenged by defense counsel on grounds that no Sponsorship Agreement existed; challenge was denied. Tier Protocol Violation confirmed on basis that prospective Sponsorship relationship constitutes sufficient connection. Perpetrator tier reduced, fifteen-year detention. Bureau classification: Sponsorship Violence — Threatening Communications.

INCI-2223-019 City: Detroit (Brightmoor district) Victim: Tier 4 Citizen, employment: medical technician, age 44 Perpetrator: Tier 1 Citizen, sponsored Citizen, month 29 of 36-month Sponsorship Period Incident: Perpetrator killed victim. Method: blunt force. Location: victim's registered secondary residence. Perpetrator turned themselves in to the nearest Arcturus Civil Security post forty-eight hours after incident. Statement: perpetrator alleged seven months of systematic financial extortion by victim, with victim demanding escalating payments as condition of co-signing the annual Tier Maintenance Attestation. Bureau note: Allegations not investigated prior to perpetrator's detention. Victim's financial records were not subpoenaed. Perpetrator received mandatory minimum sentence. Tier reduced to Tier 1, life detention recommended. Bureau classification: Sponsorship Violence — Homicide.

INCI-2224-211 City: Cleveland (Erie Remnant border district) Victim: Tier 3 Citizen, employment: administrative coordinator, age 38 Perpetrator: Tier 1 Citizen, prospective sponsored Citizen Incident: Perpetrator assaulted victim in public transit hub following victim's cancellation of Sponsorship appointment on the morning of the scheduled filing. Victim had previously verbally agreed to Sponsorship; no written agreement had been executed. Perpetrator had disclosed personal financial and housing information to victim as part of application preparation. Perpetrator apprehended. Bureau note: Assault witnessed by 14 individuals. Perpetrator did not resist arrest. No statement given. Tier reduction applied, twelve-year detention. Bureau classification: Sponsorship Violence — Assault.

---

PATTERN ANALYSIS

Of the 312 total incidents reviewed, the Statistical Integrity Division notes the following patterns:

 — 71% of incidents occurred after significant relationship investment by the perpetrator (defined as three or more months of documented contact with the victim prior to incident). — 58% of homicide incidents occurred after the Sponsorship Agreement was formally signed (i.e., during the active Sponsorship Period). — 83% of perpetrators had no prior Tier Protocol Violations or criminal conduct record. — In 67% of incidents where perpetrators made allegations of victim misconduct (coercion, financial exploitation, labor demands), no investigation of those allegations was conducted prior to sentencing. In the remaining 33%, allegations were investigated post-sentencing and no findings were made.

This Division makes no recommendation based on the above pattern data. Interpretation and policy recommendation are reserved for the Legislative Council Tier Subcommittee.

---

CONCLUSION AND POLICY CONTEXT

The 34% increase in Sponsorship Violence incidents over the 2015–2020 baseline period is consistent with trends observed following the 2018 Revision 13 changes, which extended the Sponsorship Period and increased financial surety requirements. The current revision cycle (Revision 15, deliberations 2226) may wish to consider whether the structural parameters of the Sponsorship Agreement create or amplify conditions that increase incident risk.

This memorandum does not advocate for reduction of the Sponsorship requirement. It is provided for informational context.

Annexed documents: Full incident log 2220–2225 (Tier 5 access). Perpetrator demographic breakdown (restricted). Surety recapture data by district (Tier 4 access).
